title: Analysis of Hessian Scaling for Local and Global Costs in Variational Quantum Algorithm
summary: Barren plateaus in variational quantum algorithms are typically described by gradient concentration at random initialization. In contrast, rigorous results for the Hessian, even at the level of entry-wise variance, remain limited. In this work, we analyze the scaling of Hessian-entry variances at initialization. Using exact second-order parameter-shift identities, we write $H_{jk}$ as a constant-size linear combination of shifted cost evaluations, which reduces ${\rm Var}_ρ(H_{jk})$ to a finite-dimensional covariance--quadratic form.
